title: Vending Machine
summary: Model a snack vending machine whose behaviour depends on its state: idle, collecting money, dispensing, out of stock.
description:
A vending machine sells snacks from **numbered slots**. A customer selects a product, inserts **coins or notes**, and the machine **dispenses** the product and returns **change**. An operator restocks products and collects cash.

The machine behaves very differently depending on what is happening — it should not accept money while dispensing, and it should refuse a selection that is out of stock. The company will soon add card payments.

Focus on the **state transitions** and on who is responsible for inventory, money and change.

functionalRequirements.text: The machine holds products in slots, each with a code, price and quantity.
A customer selects a product by slot code; out-of-stock selections are refused.
The customer inserts coins/notes; the machine tracks the inserted balance.
When balance ≥ price, the machine dispenses the product and returns change.
The customer can cancel before dispensing and get a full refund.
An operator can restock slots and collect cash.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: If exact change cannot be returned, the sale must be refused before dispensing.
Adding card payment must not require rewriting the state logic.

variationPoints.name: Machine state
variationPoints.description: Idle, HasMoney, Dispensing and OutOfService accept different actions.

variationPoints.name: Change-making policy
variationPoints.description: Greedy vs optimal change calculation, or limited coin stock.

extensionScenario.prompt: The company adds card payments and a 'maintenance' state in which the machine refuses all customer actions. Which classes change, which are added, and which stay untouched?

hints.title: List the states first
hints.text: Write down the states (Idle, HasMoney, Dispensing, OutOfStock/Maintenance) and which actions are legal in each. That table is your design.

hints.title: Use the State pattern
hints.text: A VendingState interface with selectProduct, insertMoney, dispense and cancel. Each state class implements only what is legal and moves the machine to the next state.

hints.title: Money is its own responsibility
hints.text: Keep change-making out of the states. A CashBox/ChangeDispenser that knows its coin stock can answer 'can I make change for X?' before dispensing (NFR-1).

curveballs.title: Cards and maintenance
curveballs.prompt: The company adds card payments and a 'maintenance' state in which the machine refuses all customer actions. Which classes change, which are added, and which stay untouched?

curveballs.title: Exact change only
curveballs.prompt: When the coin stock runs low, the machine switches to 'exact change only' and refuses payments it cannot make change for.

curveballs.title: QR code payments
curveballs.prompt: Customers can scan a QR code and pay from their phone; the machine receives a payment confirmation asynchronously.
